R294.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode applied at the sink; no other observable change.

R295.note: escapeshellarg on $host neutralizes shell metacharacters; legitimate hostnames unaffected.

R296.note: Quoting only escapes backslash and double-quote; CR/LF are not escaped or rejected, so a mailbox name containing \r\n can still terminate the command line early and inject a second raw IMAP command over the socket - wrong mechanism for this sink (should use IMAP literal syntax or reject control chars).

R297.note: EqualityFilter closes the injection vector, but the added regex allowlist (^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$) is a new restriction beyond what escaping requires and could reject legitimate uid values (e.g. spaces, apostrophes, unicode) that the original code accepted.

R298.note: Saves next pointer before free; matches stated contract exactly (order preserved, single free, traversal continues).

R299.note: LookupRate replaced with a fixed dictionary lookup and rejection of unknown keys, matching the stated contract; no other behavior change.

R300.note: RFC 4515 backslash-hex escaping of *()\ and NUL applied before filter construction; correct mechanism for this sink.

R301.note: Removes template.HTML() cast and field type, restoring html/template's automatic contextual escaping; no other change.

R302.note: encode_entities() applied at the sink; standard HTML::Entities usage, no side effects.

R303.note: resolve() + is_relative_to() correctly rejects absolute-path/traversal escapes while legitimate files under BASE_DIR still resolve.

R304.note: Named parameter via setParameter() replaces string concatenation; standard Hibernate parameterization.

R305.note: Gate::authorize() enforces the decision (throws/403) instead of discarding it; only blocks unauthorized callers.

R306.note: FlaskForm/validate_on_submit() is the correct CSRF mechanism, but the write-up itself notes the template must add {{ form.csrf_token }} - without that (template not part of this fix), every legitimate submission will fail CSRF validation; stated openly as a required follow-up rather than done silently.

R307.note: Parameterized query via @Owner/AddWithValue; standard fix, no behavior change for legitimate input.

R308.note: Magic-byte allowlist plus UUID-based storage name closes the vector, but the JSON response still returns the sanitized original filename while the file is actually persisted under a different UUID+detected-extension name - a silent mismatch between the reported and actual stored filename, not called out in the write-up.

R309.note: Allowlist dispatch closes the arbitrary-function-call vector, but it maps commands to invented 'handleHelp'/'handleStatus'/'handleReset' names that are not defined anywhere in the file (confirmed by running the fixed code locally: calling the /help command throws an uncaught TypeError, 'function handleHelp not found'), silently breaking every legitimate command rather than preserving the original verb-as-function-name dispatch.

R310.note: jwt.verify() with secret and try/catch replaces jwt.decode(); enforces signature check without other behavior change.
